html:
SMTO-WEB-0011 — The search service took too long to answer

GUID: be0d4a87-41a8-4c51-9603-73f4385b7bff
Slug: provider-timeout
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO sent your web search to the search service, but no complete answer came back within the time allowed. No search results came back from that service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you use your own search server (for example SearXNG), make sure it is running and not overloaded, and that the computer running SMTO has a working network connection. A busy, slow or unreachable server is the usual reason a search runs out of time.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities, select Configure Web, and select Test connection for that provider. One small test search shows whether the service now answers in time, without sending many searches.
  3. If the service is just slow, raise that provider's Timeout (seconds) (up to 30) and select Save. This time limit belongs to the search provider; the Model's time limits don't affect web searches.
  4. To keep working meanwhile, choose another enabled provider as Default provider, or set Fallback search to Also when the default provider fails, then select Save. SMTO can then search through a provider that answers quickly.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Connected, and a new web search returns results without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the search service. Don't send the same search over and over; it can overload a slow service further. A timeout doesn't mean the service crashed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Web search provider did not return a complete response within its configured timeout_seconds deadline.

What this means

  • The SearXNG search path catches a TimeoutError before it can return a complete result. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • The SearXNG search path catches a TimeoutError before it can return a complete result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected provider timeout and transport phase; model time limits do not govern this request.

How to fix it

  • guarded() in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/providers.py maps TimeoutError from DNS, connect or body read (bounded by the instance's settings.timeout_seconds, 1-30, default 10) to provider_timeout. Check provider health and latency from the Server host, raise timeout_seconds if appropriate, or narrow the query; model timeout settings do not control Web retrieval.
  • Inspect Web provider health and reduce the retrieval scope; model timeout settings do not control Web retrieval.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded search completes under the Web provider's configured timeout.

What not to do

  • Do not infer a provider crash from a timeout or repeatedly flood the endpoint.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
